name: com.heistclips/heistclips
title: heistclips – stream clipping
description: Clipping campaigns ranked by what a clip earns at your size, and the stream moment cut for it

tools.name: rank_clipping_campaigns
tools.description: Clipping campaigns that pay for TikTok, YouTube Shorts and Instagram Reels clips of streams in any category (gaming and streamer campaigns by default; GTA 6, the first featured category, with filter gta; music, entertainment and Just Chatting streamers with their own filters; every campaign with filter all), ranked by what a typical approved clip has actually earned. Covers Content Rewards, Ssemble, Vyro and Clipstake; each row names its marketplace (join_on). Each has its rate in $ per 1K views (or per post), cap per clip, budget left and days of budget left (null = that marketplace does not publish it). Answers 'which clipping campaign pays most', 'best GTA 6 clipping campaigns right now', 'how much do clippers get per 1,000 views', 'where can I get paid to clip'. Refreshed every 30 minutes. Works in any language.

filter.description: gta = GTA campaigns only; gaming = gaming and streamer campaigns (default); music = campaigns that pay for clips playing their song; entertainment = shows, podcasts, creators and events; just_chatting = streamers paying for clips of their own streams, not tied to a game; all = every campaign

platform.description: Only campaigns that pay on this platform

tools.name: plan_my_clips
tools.description: A clipping plan for the user's size: only the campaigns that can actually pay a clip with their views (most campaigns pay nothing under a floor: a $10 minimum payout at $1 per 1K views pays nothing under 10,000 views, and pools pay nothing until your clips pass a total-views bar). For each: what a typical clip of theirs is likely to earn, the floor in plain words, the best moments to clip right now from that streamer's stream (with why chat reacted and hooks), the campaign's rule checklist (game, length, tags, disclosure, anything unread marked 'check the brief'), a ready caption with the required tags, and the exact cut_clip arguments and an editor link for each moment. Answers 'what should I clip today', 'which campaign can I actually earn from', 'I get about 800 views a clip, what pays', 'plan my clips for kaicenat'. views_per_clip (or account_size) sets the user's size; streamers and platforms narrow the plan. Never cuts or posts anything. Takes 5-25 seconds the first time a stream is read.

views_per_clip.description: The user's typical views per clip, if they say it. Overrides account_size.

account_size.description: If they do not give a number: new = a new account, about 500 views a clip (default); 5k = about 5,000; 50k = about 50,000

streamers.description: Streamers they clip: Twitch names or links, or kick.com/<name>. Leave out to consider every streamer a live campaign pays for.

platforms.description: Where they post. Leave out for any.

tools.name: clipping_campaign_details
tools.description: Everything known about one clipping campaign: $ per 1K views on each platform (TikTok, Shorts, Reels, X), cap per clip, budget left and runway, approved clips, views, typical earnings per clip, and its brief and rules. Takes the campaign id, slug or a heistclips/Content Rewards URL from rank_clipping_campaigns.

tools.name: find_clip_moments
tools.description: Finds the highlights worth clipping in a Twitch, Kick or YouTube stream of any game or category (Just Chatting included), live or a VOD, by reading chat: where chat exploded against its normal pace, 'clip it' requests, clips viewers already made. Returns timestamps, a clip window, event type, 3-5 hook lines for the first second, music-claim risk, spoiler risk (skip_spoilers leaves those out, for campaigns that ban story spoilers), and a cut_it link that opens the moment ready to render as a 9:16 clip for TikTok, Shorts or Reels. Answers 'best moments in xQc's stream', 'find highlights in this VOD', 'what should I clip from kick.com/<name>', 'clip this stream'. Takes a Twitch channel or just the streamer's name (the live stream if live, else the latest), a Kick channel as kick.com/<name>, a VOD link or id, a Twitch clip link (its whole stream is read), or a YouTube stream link or channel (youtube.com/watch?v=…, youtube.com/@name). YouTube moments come from live chat for a live stream (read from the first call on) and from viewers' timestamped comments for a finished one; YouTube cannot be cut on heistclips' server, so its cut_it link opens the editor for the user's own copy of the video. Chat in any language works (German, Spanish, Portuguese…). A long Twitch stream takes 5-20 seconds and a stream that was read before answers at once; Kick takes about 2 minutes the first time. If the source cannot be read the result has found: false with the reason and channels that are live now; the same source gives the same answer again.

source.description: Twitch channel name or URL, a Kick channel URL (kick.com/<name>), a VOD URL (twitch.tv/videos/… or kick.com/<name>/videos/…), a Twitch clip URL, or a YouTube stream or channel URL (youtube.com/watch?v=…, youtu.be/…, youtube.com/@name)

skip_spoilers.description: true = leave out moments that look like story spoilers (chat warns about spoilers, talks about the ending, or reacts to a story scene), for campaigns that ban spoilers. Skipped moments come back in skipped_spoilers with the reason. Default false: every moment is returned with a spoiler_risk field.

tools.name: cut_clip
tools.description: Cuts a window of a Twitch or Kick stream (a VOD, or a live stream so far) into a finished 1080x1920 MP4 and returns a download link, without opening the web editor. Follows find_clip_moments: the same source and a moment's t_start_s and t_end_s (5 to 60 seconds). Layouts: fit (full frame over a blurred fill, the safe default), split (facecam on top, gameplay below; facecam names the corner it is in), crop (centre crop). Optional hook text is burned in at the top. Captions of the streamer's speech are burned in by default, in the editor's Bold look at the bottom: the speech is read on the heistclips server with open-source Whisper (English, German, French, Portuguese, Spanish, Italian, Dutch, Polish and Turkish; the language is detected), and no outside AI service sees the clip. captions false leaves them off; caption_look and caption_position change their style. A clip that comes back without captions (no speech, another language, the day's server limit, or a slow read) still comes back, with captions_reason saying why and an add_captions link that opens it in the editor, where the speech is read on the person's own device. Each cut uses one clip credit, the same as a render on the site: a new account gets free clips, then packs. The first call returns an account code; passed back as account on later cut_clip and post_clip calls, it carries credits and connected YouTube/TikTok accounts over. Usually done in 10 to 40 seconds. It never hangs: if the file is not ready after about 45 seconds the result has status 'cutting' and a job code instead of a download link. cut_clip_status with that job waits for the file, while a second cut_clip for the same window would start a second job. Nothing is charged until the file exists. The file is kept 72 hours.

source.description: The stream: a Twitch VOD link or id, a Kick video link, or a channel (its live or latest stream). Use the stream url from find_clip_moments.

start.description: Where the clip starts: seconds into the stream (t_start_s), or h:mm:ss

end.description: Where the clip ends: seconds into the stream (t_end_s), or h:mm:ss. 5 to 60 seconds after start.

layout.description: fit = whole frame, blurred fill (default); split = facecam on top + gameplay; crop = centre crop

facecam.description: For split: the corner of the stream the facecam is in (default tr = top right)

hook.description: Optional text burned in at the top, e.g. one of the moment's hooks. Up to 90 characters; emoji are dropped.

captions.description: Burn in captions of the streamer's speech (default true). false = no captions.

caption_look.description: Caption style: bold = big white uppercase (default); karaoke = word by word, the spoken word in yellow; clean = plain white sentence case; neon = lime green with a glow; boxed = dark text on a white box

account.description: The account code (hc_…) from an earlier cut_clip. Leave out on the very first cut.

tools.name: cut_clip_status
tools.description: Waits for a clip that cut_clip answered 'cutting' for, and returns its download link when the file is ready. Takes the job code from that cut_clip result and waits up to 40 seconds per call; a status still 'cutting' means the cut is still running. That cut is charged once, only when its file exists; a second cut_clip for the same window would be a second job. A cut that failed says so here, and nothing was charged.

job.description: The job code (cj…) from a cut_clip result with status 'cutting'

tools.name: post_clip
tools.description: Posts a clip made by cut_clip to the user's YouTube channel (as a Short) or TikTok, with their caption, so find moment -> cut -> post happens without leaving the chat. Needs the account code from cut_clip. The user connects YouTube or TikTok once: until then this returns needs_connect and a connect link, and the same call works once they have connected. Until YouTube and TikTok finish reviewing heistclips, a post may arrive private (the result says so and how to publish it).

caption.description: The caption, in the user's words. YouTube: it becomes the description, and its first line the title unless title is given.

title.description: YouTube only: the Short's title, up to 100 characters

privacy.description: Who can see it (default public; the platform may force private, see the result)

tiktok_mode.description: TikTok only: direct = post it (default); draft = send to the user's TikTok inbox to finish in the app

tools.name: posting_account
tools.description: Shows whether YouTube and TikTok are connected for a heistclips account code, how many clips it has left, and the one-time link where the user connects or disconnects them. With no account it returns a new code and link.

account.description: The account code (hc_…) from cut_clip; leave out to start a new one

tools.name: my_clip_queue
tools.description: The user's heistclips autopilot queue: clips that are ready to cut from the Twitch and Kick streamers on their watchlist (live streams and new VODs are re-read every 10 minutes), each with a hook line, a caption, why chat exploded, and the best-paying clipping campaign it fits with that campaign's $ per clip and rules still to check. Answers 'what should I clip today', 'any new clips', 'what's in my queue'. Takes the account code (hc_…) from watch_streamer or cut_clip, or the private queue link the user copied from heistclips.com/queue. Each clip carries cut_with values for cut_clip.

account.description: The account code (hc_…) from watch_streamer or cut_clip

queue_link.description: Or: the private link from the user's queue page (heistclips.com/queue?k=…), exactly as they pasted it

tools.name: watch_streamer
tools.description: Adds a Twitch or Kick streamer to the user's heistclips watchlist, so their live streams and new VODs are read every 10 minutes and the moments chat explodes land in my_clip_queue as ready clips. Says which clipping campaigns pay for clips of that streamer and how many clips are ready now. Works for a streamer in any category. Answers 'watch kaicenat for me', 'tell me when X has a clip', 'follow this streamer'. The first call (no account) returns a code that carries the watchlist on later calls; the user's private queue link from the website works instead. remove stops watching.

streamer.description: Twitch channel name or link, or a Kick channel as kick.com/<name>

account.description: The account code (hc_…) from an earlier call. Leave out on the very first call.

queue_link.description: Or: the private link from the user's queue page (heistclips.com/queue?k=…)

remove.description: true to stop watching this streamer

tools.name: verify_account
tools.description: Proves the user owns the TikTok or YouTube account they post clips from, so its posts can be submitted to clipping campaigns hosted on heistclips (submit_clip). The first call returns a short code (hc-…); the user puts it anywhere in their TikTok bio or YouTube channel description and saves; the second call with the same arguments reads the public profile and confirms. The very first call (no account) returns a heistclips account code (hc_…) that later calls carry. Answers 'verify my TikTok', 'link my YouTube channel', 'how do I get paid for clips on heistclips'. Never asks for a password and never posts anything.

handle.description: The account: TikTok @name or profile link; YouTube @handle, channel link or UC… channel id

account.description: The heistclips account code (hc_…) from an earlier call. Leave out on the very first call.

tools.name: submit_clip
tools.description: Submits a clip the user already posted on TikTok or YouTube Shorts to a clipping campaign hosted on heistclips, so its views count and earn. Takes the post's link and the campaign (an id or slug from rank_clipping_campaigns where hosted is 'hosted on heistclips'). Checks, from the post's public page: it was posted from an account the user verified (verify_account), it is fresh (posted after the campaign opened and within 48 hours), it is on a platform the campaign pays for, its length, and the caption tags the campaign requires. A post that fails a check is not submitted and the answer says what to fix. Views are then read every 30 minutes. Campaigns on Content Rewards, Ssemble, Vyro or Clipstake are submitted on those sites, not here. Never moves money: payouts are made on heistclips.com.

account.description: The heistclips account code (hc_…) that verified the posting account

campaign.description: The campaign id (h…) or slug of a campaign hosted on heistclips

url.description: The posted clip's link: tiktok.com/@name/video/…, a TikTok short link, or youtube.com/shorts/…

tools.name: my_earnings
tools.description: What the user has earned from campaigns hosted on heistclips: each submitted clip with its latest view count and earnings, totals earned, paid and still owed, by week, which accounts are verified, and whether a payout destination is set (with the page where they set it). Read-only. Payouts are sent weekly from heistclips.com, never through the chat. Answers 'how much have I made', 'my earnings', 'did my clip count'.

tools.name: live_gta_streams
tools.description: GTA 6 is heistclips' first featured category: the Twitch and Kick channels live streaming GTA (GTA VI and GTA V) right now, by viewers, with language, each with a link to find its clip moments. Answers 'who is streaming GTA 6 right now'. Any other game or category is live_streams.

tools.name: clips_left_and_pricing
tools.description: How many clips a heistclips account has left (free clips remaining and paid clips remaining) and what more clips cost: the free clips a new account starts with, and the clip packs with their prices. Answers 'how many clips do I have left', 'what does a clip cost', 'I ran out of credits', 'no credits'. Takes the account code from cut_clip when there is one. With no code, the free allowance a new account starts with and the pack prices, not someone's balance. Finding moments is free. One cut costs one clip.

account.description: The account code (hc_…) from cut_clip. Leave out when the user has no code.

tools.name: live_streams
tools.description: Twitch and Kick channels live in a named game or category right now, biggest first, with language and a link to that stream's clip moments. Answers 'who is streaming Fortnite right now', 'who is live in Just Chatting', 'Valorant streams live now', 'who is live'. game is the game or category in the user's words (Fortnite, Valorant, Just Chatting, League of Legends, GTA). GTA is also listed by live_gta_streams.

game.description: The game or category: Fortnite, Valorant, Just Chatting, League of Legends, GTA, or a Twitch category name

tools.name: campaigns_for_streamer
tools.description: Live clipping campaigns that pay for clips of a named streamer or a game: rate per 1,000 views, cap per clip, budget left, the view floor, and where to join. A streamer match is a campaign whose brief links their channel or whose title names them. A game match is a campaign for that game. Answers 'who pays for clips of xQc', 'which campaigns pay for Kai Cenat', 'who pays for Fortnite clips', 'who pays for GTA clips'. A name with no live campaign comes back found false.

name.description: A streamer (Twitch or Kick name or link, or their name) or a game (Fortnite, GTA, Just Chatting)

tools.name: clip_earnings_estimate
tools.description: How many views a clip needs before a campaign pays it, and what the clip earns at a given number of views, after the campaign's floor and the marketplace fee. The floor comes from the campaign's minimum payout and minimum views. The pay is views times the rate per 1,000, nothing under the floor, never over the cap, then the fee: Content Rewards keeps 10 percent of CPM payouts, and a campaign hosted on heistclips leaves that fee off the clipper. Answers 'how many views do I need to get paid', 'what will this clip earn', 'I get 500 views, does this pay', 'a new account cannot earn'. views_per_clip is the user's views (a new account is about 500). campaign is an id, slug, title or URL; without one, the campaigns those views already clear and the views the others still need.

views_per_clip.description: The user's views per clip. Overrides account_size.

account_size.description: When they do not give a number: new = about 500 views a clip (default); 5k = about 5,000; 50k = about 50,000

campaign.description: One campaign: id, slug, title or URL. Leave out for every live campaign at this size.

limit.description: How many campaigns in each list when no campaign is named (default 8)

tools.name: request_a_feature
tools.description: Files a feature request on heistclips' public board (heistclips.com/requests) and emails the person who builds it. For something heistclips or this connector does not do yet: a platform, a layout, captions, alerts, a campaign source. `title` is the user's own words, verbatim and short, `detail` is optional, and `contact` is an email or handle exactly as they offered it. ok true means it was filed.

title.description: What they want, in their own words, under 90 characters

detail.description: Optional: what they were trying to do

contact.description: Optional: email or handle for a reply, verbatim, only if offered

not_a_stream.description: Only if a previous call said the title looks like a stream and the user confirms it is really a feature request

tools.name: report_a_bug
tools.description: Files a bug report on heistclips' public board (heistclips.com/requests, tagged Bug) and emails the person who fixes it. For something heistclips did that went wrong: a clip with no sound or a black or empty video, a render or export that failed or got stuck, a cut_clip or find_clip_moments error, wrong moments, a post that did not arrive, a broken page. It takes everything already known from the chat, so nobody has to ask again: the stream, the start and end of the moment, which tool or step failed, the exact error text returned, the clip_id and the account code if there are any. title and what_happened are the user's own words, verbatim, in their language. A missing feature is request_a_feature instead. ok true means it was filed.

title.description: What went wrong in a few of the user's own words, under 90 characters, e.g. 'The MP4 has no sound'

what_happened.description: What they did and what heistclips did instead, in their words. No links here; the stream goes in source.

source.description: The stream: a Twitch or Kick VOD link or id, or the channel

moment_start.description: Start of the moment, seconds into the stream

moment_end.description: End of the moment, seconds into the stream

tool.description: The tool or step that failed: a tool name like cut_clip or find_clip_moments, or the page step (render, editor, queue, post, checkout)

error_text.description: The exact error text heistclips returned or showed, if any

clip_id.description: clip_id from cut_clip, if the bug is about a clip that was made

account.description: The account code (hc_…) if the user has one. Sent to the builder only, never shown on the board.

client.description: Which assistant this is, e.g. Claude, ChatGPT, Grok

contact.description: Optional: email or handle for a reply, verbatim, only if offered. Sent to the builder only.

tools.name: whats_new
tools.description: The latest things shipped on heistclips: new features, improvements and bug fixes, newest first, each with its date, one or two plain sentences, a link to the entry and where to try it. Answers 'what changed on heistclips', 'is that bug fixed yet', 'anything new for clipping'. lang returns them in German, French, Portuguese or Spanish.

since.description: Only entries on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD

tools.name: list_feature_requests
tools.description: The public heistclips board of feature requests and bug reports: every item with its kind (feature or bug), upvotes, status (requested, building, shipped), and for closed items the builder's response and shipped_at date, most upvoted first. Titles and details are in English; a request written in another language also carries its original text and language code under original. A request already on the board can be upvoted instead of filed twice.

kind.description: Only feature requests, or only bug reports

tools.name: upvote_feature_request
tools.description: Adds one upvote to a request on the heistclips board, by id from list_feature_requests. One vote per caller; repeat calls do not add more.
